notes.3c: Comprehensive responses • Candidates described the features (often with the help of a clear, labelled diagram) and explained how they are formed. • Candidates wrote in detail, linking ideas together (for example speed of flow reducing which leads to the deposition of the load) or developing each idea. • Candidates used geographical terminology to describe the features of a delta (for example distributaries) and the processes responsible for their formation (for example flocculation). notes.4a: (i) Comprehensive responses • This question was well answered with almost all candidates giving the correct answer. [Limited responses] • There were too few responses to provide a meaningful comment.

notes.key_messages:
What candidates did well
• Candidates followed the rubric correctly, answering three questions only, one chosen from each of
Sections A, B and C.
• Candidates responded appropriately to command words and words which indicated the focus and
context of each question.
• Candidates showed excellent knowledge and understanding of the topics being assessed.
• Candidates used accurate geographical terminology in answers, especially when referring to processes.
• Candidates used extended writing where appropriate, linking relevant ideas or developing them fully.
• Candidates planned their answers and organised extended responses logically.
• Candidates were able to use and interpret a range of different types of geographical sources to support
ideas expressed in answers.
• Candidates wrote clearly and precisely, avoiding vague words or statements.
• Candidates selected suitable case studies where required in part (c) questions, including relevant detail
and place specific information whilst succinctly answering the question set.
What candidates needed to improve
• Candidates need to read questions more carefully and ensure that they answer the questions asked.
• Candidates need to make sure they respond correctly to the command word (for example: describe,
explain, compare).
• Candidates need to avoid answering using bullet points, especially where extended answers are
• Candidates need to avoid using vague words and terms, such as services, pollution, overcrowding and
resources.
• In part (c) questions candidates need to make sure that irrelevant detail is not included, such as detailed
general introductions describing the location.
